cross_lane_referrals.disposition: Bilingual private missal manuscripts 1199/1201/1202 belong to translation history. Latin Missale Canonicum based on Beauvais 1756, plus a 1757 proper supplement, are original source-state leads. Amiet did not locate a copy; this is not proof of global absence.
Mass chant components include two 1737 temporal volumes, 1739 sanctoral and ca.1740 fragment; a 1738 book mixes offices and Masses. These do not establish cathedral Lyon missal recensions.
Festal missal ca.1480 (Chalon-sur-Saône 148) is Augustinian canonical use; no cathedral recension inferred.
A 1531 printed missal preserves historical abbey use; the 1520 book is a breviary. Refer to monastic lane.

BnF n.a.lat.3042 breviary has added votive Masses at fol.54; a fourteenth-century festal missal is Lons-le-Saunier 10; Paris Assemblée Nationale 10 is ca.1490. Refer as local monastic Eucharistic witnesses.
Thirteenth-century missal in Collection Thiollier has fifteenth-century additions; refer to monastic lane.
Three fragmentary missal witnesses date to the fifteenth century, turn of fifteenth/sixteenth centuries, and second half of eleventh century. Refer to monastic lane.
Ambrosiana M.70 sup. ca.1160 and Parkminster A.33 twelfth-century graduals are Carthusian Mass chant components. The Milan holding location does not make M.70 Ambrosian use.
Getty Ludwig V 5 missal, dated 1254–1262, requires Dominican-lane accounting; no cathedral Lyon recension inferred.
The 1776 festal gradual SM 007 is a local Franciscan Mass chant component.
